# Venom v0.9.0-alpha

> **Historical release notice:** these immutable binaries predate the current
> remediated source tree and its bounded default runtime. They are not an
> installation path for the behavior documented on the current branch. See
> [Distribution](../../docs/DISTRIBUTION.md) before evaluating any artifact.

Venom is a modular Rust-based penetration-testing framework focused on research and extensibility. This is the first public alpha release: APIs remain unstable, the project has not completed an independent security audit, and it is not production-ready.

Use Venom only on systems you own or have explicit permission to test.

## Added

- Multi-phase asynchronous scanner with structured findings and lifecycle events.
- Source-level Preview plugin contract with explicit API-line compatibility.
- `ScannerSdk` builder for application-defined scan phases.
- CLI, API adapter, proxy, Lua, reporting, distributed, anomaly, and dashboard modules.
- Criterion benchmarks, parser fuzz targets, CodeQL, dependency policy, MSRV checks, and published engineering documentation.
- Plugin and scanner starter projects generated through `cargo xtask`.

## Changed

- Shared event and finding contracts now live in `venom-core`.
- Documentation separates implemented behavior from roadmap and Preview surfaces.
- Internal crate dependencies carry explicit prerelease version requirements.

## Fixed

- Version output derives from Cargo metadata.
- Release archives have unique platform names and published SHA256 checksums.
- The unused, unmaintained `rustls-pemfile` dependency was removed.

## Security

- Responsible disclosure, supported-version, CVE, response-target, and researcher-credit policies are documented in `SECURITY.md`.
- Release archives receive GitHub build-provenance attestations.
- No independent security audit has been completed.

## Historical artifacts

The attached archives describe only this historical release. If retained for
reproducibility, verify an archive against its `SHA256SUMS` entry before
extraction. Do not infer current source behavior from those binaries; the
repository has no supported installer or current binary channel.

## Known gaps

- Plugin and Scanner SDK APIs may change during the `0.x` line.
- Endpoint-scale performance, mutation score, and external audit evidence are not yet published.
- The HTTP adapter currently exposes only its documented health route and startup hook.
